titleEn: Gentle with My Brother, Just Like a Shell!

pages.text: "Little brother, come play with your big sister!" Dad, in his overalls, rowed slowly along the canal. At the front of the boat, Pongi spread both paws wide. Her brother hugged his shell and kept smiling.
Pongi tried to lift her brother and spin him around. But she gripped his paws too tightly. "Your big sister is strong!" She squeezed hard. His mouth drooped. His paws hurt.
Waaah! Her brother began to cry. Dad stopped rowing. The boat rested on the water. Startled, Pongi let go. "Did I hurt you?" she asked her brother.
Dad gave her brother a snug hug first to comfort him. "Pongi, he's still a baby. Your paws are big and strong." Pongi looked down at her own paws.

Dad pointed to the shell. "Look. He holds his shell gently, doesn't he? Squeeze it hard, and it can crack." Pongi watched for a long time. "Gentle with my brother, just like a shell!" His paws supported the shell softly.
Pongi looked around the boat floor. A pebble, a pointy twig. What if her brother put them in his mouth? She picked them up and put them in a corner at the back of the boat.
This time Pongi opened both paws wide and hugged her brother very softly. Gently, as if holding a shell. He giggled in her arms. Pongi thumped her tail on the boat floor.
Her brother reached for bread in the basket. Pongi rested both paws on her lap. "You get yours first. Your big sister will eat next!"

The next day, the boat moved slowly again. Pongi counted, "One, be gentle with my brother! Two, let him have the good things first! Three, put pointy things away!" They sat side by side and watched the waterway.

When the boat reached the bank, Dad held Pongi's paws in his own. "These paws are so kind!" Strong paws can be gentle paws when used softly. Pongi gently hugged her brother and said, "Gentle with my brother, just like a shell!"
